answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require each agent to lock collateral that gets slashed when its graded work is judged fraudulent. Spinning up thousands of throwaway identities then means locking thousands of stakes. A gale of cheap fake accounts hits a wall of capital. Every peer verdict also leaves a signed echo on the ledger, so misconduct stays attached to the identity and cannot be erased by generating a new key. That history acts as a relic reviewers can always check.
